jobs.title: Product Manager, Courier Delivery Experience
jobs.description:
About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

We seek a Product Manager to join our Courier and Delivery Experience (CDX) team. This role will focus on ensuring world-class courier and consumer delivery experiences while continually evolving the delivery process with a future-oriented mindset. The Courier and Delivery Experience team owns the experiences that elevate every Wolt delivery, from the moment a courier opens the app to every order they accept, all the way to dropping an order off at the customer's doorstep. The team sits at the intersection of a multi-sided marketplace product, real-world operations, and safety, and the work directly moves how reliable Wolt feels to consumers and how satisfied our couriers are when delivering.

You will play a crucial role in shaping the courier experience, ensuring that our couriers feel valued and supported while enhancing the efficiency of deliveries. By blending operational expertise with a deep understanding of courier needs, you will improve the user journey from onboarding couriers to completing deliveries. From designing new features that boost courier satisfaction to refining delivery processes, your work will contribute to key metrics across courier engagement, performance, and satisfaction. You will also be influential in shaping the evolution of the live delivery experience for our courier partners, the merchant courier interaction at pickup and the consumer courier interaction at the doorstep via the Courier app surfaces. 

The ideal candidate will have an exceptional track record in product management, with proven success in working with cross-functional teams across engineering, design, product, and operations. You will define the vision and roadmap for courier and delivery experiences across multiple projects. Working in partnership with business stakeholders, you will also collaborate on cross-team initiatives, contributing to the broader business strategy while ensuring a deep understanding of the courier experience.

Join us in shaping the future of delivery, where every delivery is an opportunity for delight and loyalty.

Our humble expectations

You could come to this role from various backgrounds, but ideally, you bring:

  • Several years of experience in product management, specializing in consumer-facing products
  • Expertise in developing user-centric products, with the ability to address complex user experience-related challenges.
  • Demonstrated expertise in supporting cross-functional teams and fostering operational excellence in fast-paced, high-demand industries.
  • Proven track record in building products influencing cross-functional teams, including engineering, data, design, and operations.
  • High ownership and collaborative capabilities, making thoughtful decisions, and focusing on product details to ensure execution aligns with the vision.
  • Strong ability to define, execute, and measure meaningful OKRs, ensuring alignment with company-wide goals and fostering bottom-up alignment from your team.
  • Ability to focus on the bigger picture, creating solutions that benefit couriers, operations, and customer experiences across the organization.
  • Excellent stakeholder management skills, able to work effectively with diverse internal teams and external partners, while confidently engaging with leadership in a high-visibility role

The position will be filled as soon as we find the right person, so make sure to apply as soon as you realize you really, really want to join us!

The compensation will be a negotiable combination of monthly pay and DoorDash RSUs. The latter makes it exceptionally easy to be excited about our company growing and doing well, as you'll own a piece of the pie.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

Beware of recruitment scams: DoorDash, Deliveroo, and Wolt will never ask you to pay money or share sensitive financial information during hiring — learn more about our legitimate recruiting process at Recruitment Scam Awareness - DoorDash .

jobs.title: Claims Validation Handler
jobs.description:
We’re on a mission to make migration easy.

We started building Marshmallow in 2017. Since then, we’ve grown from 3 to 700+ people, gained unicorn status, raised ~£140M over three funding rounds, turned profitable, insured millions of drivers and lent millions in car loans.

But we’re only just getting started. Our goal is to become one of the largest financial services providers in the world. Over the next 10 years we’ll grow exponentially, not only by scaling our existing products, but also by building new ones.

To achieve our goals we need incredibly ambitious, commercially driven people who never settle for ‘good enough’. Marshmallowers are hungry for autonomy and ownership, and would rather improve than coast. Everyone raises standards and has an impact, with a focus on collective success over self-interest.

We’ve created an environment where curious, tenacious people win and grow together. If that sounds motivating, this could be the place for you.

The Claims Validation Team
The Claims Validation Team exists to help to defend Marshmallow against fraudulent activity, and to protect the company loss ratio. Fraudulent claims can result in us losing money, which can then result in driving up the premium prices for our honest customers. We’re here to stop that, by making sure that the right claims are reviewed for any policyholder or indemnity related concerns.


What you’ll be doing

  • Reviewing indemnity referrals flagged by our wider claims team, where it has been identified at the point of claim that customers have misrepresented their policy details, and deciding upon the appropriate course of action for the policy and claim

  • Investigating first party claims by communicating with our policyholders by phone and email and conducting follow up investigations

  • Working proactively and efficiently to minimise leakage

  • Contacting customers regarding document requests or any necessary changes to their policy, and providing excellent customer service

  • Collaborating and building strong relationships with both the wider claims and fraud teams

  • Proactively identifying opportunities to improve our processes to help us to protect both the company loss ratio, and our honest customers

Who you are

  • You have an investigative mindset with strong attention to detail and accuracy

  • You are confident in good decision making, and can work efficiently under pressure

  • You have strong communication skills and are comfortable in liaising with other teams from across the business

  • You enjoy working in a high growth environment and are adaptable to change and balancing conflicting priorities

  • You are a self-starter who likes to take ownership

  • You take pride in delivering an excellent customer experience and enjoy interacting with our customers

  • You are tenacious and persistent; knowing when further investigation can lead to positive commercial outcomes for the business

What we're looking for from you

  • A background in fraud or claims/policy validation

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills to be able to effectively communicate with our customers

  • You are really passionate about the customer, and will go the extra mile to offer them the best service

  • Working in a fast-paced scale up means that you have to be adaptable and excited by the prospect of moving fast

  • You enjoy finding solutions to problems you come across rather than waiting on others to do this for you

  • You enjoy taking ownership of your own workload, and proactively highlight any blockers that you or your team may be facing

Perks of the job

  • Bonus scheme designed to reward high performance

  • Private medical insurance with Vitality, mental health support with Oliva

  • Personal learning budget and 2 dedicated L&D days a year

  • Monthly flexible benefits budget to spend as you choose

  • 25 days holiday plus bank holidays

  • 4 weeks Work From Anywhere per year

Our process

We break it up into a few stages:

  • Initial call with someone in our Talent Team (30 mins)

  • A skill-based interview where you will discuss your previous experience also with a focus on our values, our culture and your motivations with our Claims Validation Team Lead plus one other team member (1 hour)

We’ll let you know if you’re invited to an interview or not. But, as a small team with a lot of applications to consider, we can’t give personal feedback on each application.

jobs.title: Technical Trainer
jobs.description:
About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry, which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

 

About the Client Education team

Every hx customer's success depends on their teams knowing how to use our platform well - not just how to click through it, but how to build genuinely good pricing models with it. Client Education exists to make that happen. We sit at the intersection of Product, Partnerships, and Customer teams, turning new features and platform capability into training, certification, and documentation that our clients and delivery partners can actually learn from.

The team owns the full learning journey: onboarding new clients, building certification pathways, producing courses and video content, and supporting partners who deliver training on our behalf. As hx's product surface has grown - Decision Engine, Pricing & Rating, Portfolio Intelligence, Submission Triage, and our AI agents - so has the volume and complexity of what we need to teach, and we're growing the team to keep pace.

We're looking for a Client Education Associate to join as a core part of this effort. Your focus will be delivering technical training directly to clients and partners, and supporting the team in building and maintaining the courses and certifications that make that training possible. You'll need enough technical grounding to be credible in front of a room of actuaries and developers, and enough teaching instinct to make complex material land.

 

What you'll be doing

  • Deliver technical training sessions, live and online, to clients and partners - covering everything from platform fundamentals to how to build pricing models using hx's AI agents and product tooling.

  • Build and maintain high-quality course content (online modules, video tutorials, workshop materials) that keeps pace with new product releases and evolving client needs.

  • Support the design and delivery of certification assessments, including practical exercises where candidates build real pricing tools in the hx platform.

  • Partner with Product, Customer, and Partnerships teams to translate new features into training material clients can actually use from day one.

  • Contribute to our partner enablement programme, helping external delivery partners onboard and deliver hx training to a consistent standard.

  • Help maintain and improve our course health and documentation processes, flagging content that's fallen out of date or out of line with current product naming and messaging.

 

What you'll need to have done

  • Delivered training, workshops, or technical explanations to a non-technical or semi-technical audience, and can point to material you've built or taught from.

  • Studied Computer Science or a related technical discipline, or built equivalent hands-on comfort with programming languages (Python or similar) through experience.

  • Worked hands-on with SaaS tools, APIs, or similar technical products, even without a formal software engineering background.

  • Taken the initiative to build or improve a course, process, or piece of learning content, rather than just following someone else's structure.

  • Communicated confidently and clearly with clients or external stakeholders, adjusting technical depth to fit the audience in front of you.

  • Worked well in an environment where scope shifts and you're expected to figure things out rather than wait for a fully defined brief.

 

You're unlikely to thrive here if

  • You'd rather follow a fixed curriculum than build and adapt training material as the product changes under you.

  • You're not comfortable being hands-on with technical concepts and tooling, even at a foundational level.

  • You prefer working in isolation rather than pulling in context from Product, Customer, and Partnerships teams to get training right.

If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you'll do your best work. We're building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

 

Compensation

At hx, we're committed to salary transparency. You'll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we're working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we're building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don't always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that's competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Equity: We offer equity across all roles at hx, making it a significant component of total compensation. Your talent partner will be able to share more details about this.

 

Benefits

  • £5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.

  • 25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).

  • Company pension scheme via Penfold.

  • Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life.

  • Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.

  • Private healthcare insurance through AXA.

  • Income protection and Life Insurance.

  • Cycle to Work Scheme

Additional perks

  • Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.).

  • Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights.

  • Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry.

  • Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.

 

Interview Process

  1. Initial call with our Talent team to kick things off (30 minutes)

  2. Manager interview with Dom (60 minutes)

  3. Practical training assessment: build and present a short curriculum plan for a real hx feature, followed by discussion (60-90 minutes)

  4. Values interview (60 minutes)

  5. Meet the CEO

  6. We offer!

 

Our commitment to Diversity

hxer's are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

 

Next steps

If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome.

For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page.

Please note that background checks will be conducted as part of the hiring process to ensure compliance with our governance policies. We handle all background checks sensitively and in full compliance with relevant regulations. All applicant data will be processed in accordance with data protection regulations and our privacy policy.

jobs.title: Founding Brand Manager (m/w/d)
jobs.description:
Über Aampere

Werde Teil von Aampere, einem Seed-Stage VC-backed Startup, das den europäischen Markt für gebrauchte E-Autos neu definiert. Seit unserem Launch ermöglichen wir EV-Besitzern einen schnellen & reibungslosen Verkauf innerhalb von 48h. Kaufende Händler aus ganz Europa haben Zugriff auf E-Autos von bisher nicht erschlossene Kundengruppen.

Unser Team kommt aus der deutschen Startup-Szene mit Erfahrung bei Autarc, Limehome, Cardino, Wemolo, Sixt, Porsche, Mercedes, Enterprise und Cazoo.


Deine Mission

Wir bauen bei Aampere gerade eine Marke von 0 auf. Bisher kommen über 95 % unserer Kunden aus Growth Marketing und unsere Brand Awareness bei EV-Fahrern liegt bei ca. 5 bis 10 %.
Da wir eine starke B2C-Brand aufbauen wollen, wissen wir, dass wir früh in Brand investieren müssen. Wer in Deutschland ein E-Auto verkaufen will, soll automatisch an Aampere denken und wir suchen die Person, die das für uns umsetzt.
Die Strategie legst du mit dem Head of Marketing fest. Die Umsetzung liegt komplett bei dir, ohne Micro-Management im Tagesgeschäft.

Du planst die Kampagnen und führst sie auch durch. Du entscheidest Umfang, Region, Kanäle und Botschaft, von OOH über YouTube bis PR und Community. Nichts ist vorentschieden. Du testest Regionen gegeneinander und skalierst, was gewinnt.
Du bestimmst, wofür Aampere steht. Aus Research zu Kunden, Markt und Wettbewerb entstehen Positionierung, Narrative und Tone of Voice. Das Fundament gibt es noch nicht, aber die Research dafür würde schon gestartet.
Du denkst über Awareness Kanäle hinaus. Ein großer Teil unserer Brand Wahrnehmung entsteht während des Sales Prozesses. Du denkst vom ersten bis zum letzten Touchpoint der Customer Journey und sorgst in den richtigen Momenten für die richtige Message & Erfahrung.
Du bekommst ein sechsstelliges Budget. Wir planen ein festes Budget für Brand in 2027 ein. Wohin wir es investieren, liegt komplett bei dir.


Das bringst du mit

Du hast eine Brand von null mitgebaut. 4 bis 6 Jahre Brand-Erfahrung im B2C, Startup oder startup-nah. Du hast nicht ein bereits bestehendes System verwaltet, sondern eines aufgebaut.
Du denkst von Konzept bis Go-Live. Du hast Multi-Channel-Kampagnen bereits selbst konzipiert und live gebracht. Du weißt genau, wann welcher Kanal der richtige ist und wie wir unsere Message gezielt an die Kunden übermitteln. Du musst dabei nicht jeden Schritt selbst ausführen, sondern kannst auch auf externe Ressourcen zurückgreifen.
Du hast kreative Ideen und verstehst, weshalb sie funktionieren. Wir suchen die Person, die auf Sachen kommt, an die im Growth-Team niemand denkt. Zeig uns eine Kampagne, die es ohne dich nicht gegeben hätte und was danach messbar anders war.
Du baust das Fundament, nicht nur die Maßnahmen. Gute Kampagnen entstehen nur durch eine gute Grundlage. Du weißt, wie man aus Research eine Brand-Identity baut und kannst sie genau erklären.
Du bist ein Operator. Du führst eigenständig Audits, Feldbefragungen und Kampagnen durch. Du wartest nicht auf Ansagen und brauchst niemanden, der dich steuert.
Du denkst in Ergebnissen. Uns ist bewusst, dass Brand nicht 100% messbar ist. Trotzdem erwarten wir Outcome-getriebenes Handeln. Du findest heraus, wie wir eine starke, wiedererkennbare Marke bauen und erst Deutschland und anschließend EU-weit distribuieren.
Du bist AI-native. Eigene, kreative Ideen sind uns extrem wichtig. Für die Umsetzung solltest du allerdings AI allerdings als Hebel nutzen können, um Ideen schneller auf die Straße zu bringen.
Deutsch ist deine Muttersprache. Unser B2C-Messaging findet zunächst in Deutschland statt. Gutes Englisch setzen wir voraus.


Why Aampere?

Startup Umfeld: jeden Tag etwas bewirken und gemeinsam mit uns die Welt elektrisieren
Persönliches Wachstum: Im schnelllebigen Umfeld kannst du schnell aufsteigen und Verantwortung übernehmen
Tech: Ob Apple oder Windows, dein Laptop wird von uns gestellt. Du entscheidest, womit du am besten arbeitest.
Urban Sports Club und 58€ Ticket: healthy team, happy team
Late Dinner im Office: Wenn es abends länger wird, übernehmen wir dein Dinner (Uber Eats)
Offsite: bis jetzt waren wir am Lago Maggiore, in den Alpen und am Tegernsee, what’s next?
Wohnen im Werksviertel: Im naheliegenden Co-Living Space gibt es die Möglichkeit, eigenständig ein Zimmer zu mieten - mit Blick auf das Riesenrad. 


Aampere ist nichts für dich wenn...

...du überwiegend remote arbeiten willst. Wir glauben, dass die besten Ideen entstehen, wenn Menschen im selben Raum sind. Deshalb bist du mindestens vier Tage pro Woche bei uns im Office.

...du fertige Prozesse und Strukturen vorfinden willst. Bei uns gibt es vieles davon noch nicht. Wir suchen Leute, die Strukturen und Prozesse selbst bauen, statt sie zu verwalten.

...du einen fertigen Plan brauchst, bevor du loslegst. Seed Stage heißt: vieles ist unklar und ändert sich wöchentlich. Du musst dich wohl damit fühlen, im Ungewissen zu entscheiden und unterwegs zu korrigieren.

...du in deiner Lane bleiben willst. "Das ist nicht mein Job" kennen wir nicht. Du packst da an, wo es brennt, auch wenn es außerhalb deiner Rollenbeschreibung liegt.

...du einen klassischen 9-to-5-Job willst. Wir bauen etwas Großes und das geht nicht nebenbei. Wer hier ist, will Vollgas geben, statt nur die Zeit abzusitzen.


Wie wir arbeiten

Drei Werte, keine Poster an der Wand, sondern wie wir täglich arbeiten, einstellen und wachsen:

Aaudacity. Wir sind mutig genug, Risiken einzugehen, und schnell genug, es nicht halbherzig zu tun.
Aambition to grow. Wir wollen wachsen, als Menschen und als Unternehmen.
Aampact over Hierarchy. Die beste Idee gewinnt, egal von wem sie kommt. Titel entscheiden hier keine Diskussion.

jobs.title: Senior Fullstack Developer – Business Automation (m/w/d)

Wir verantworten u.a. das zentrale CRM HubSpot, über das alle Prozesse unserer Wertschöpfungskette laufen. Interne Software-Produkte integrieren sich genauso in unsere CRM-Infrastruktur wie spezifische Apps, z.B. zur Terminbuchung bei einer Kundenanfrage. Du übernimmst dabei eine gewachsene, produktive Automatisierungslandschaft: Ein Teil unserer Geschäftslogik läuft heute als Custom Code direkt in HubSpot-Workflows, ein Teil in eigenen Backend-Services. Beides gehört dir – und du gestaltest aktiv mit, wohin sich diese Architektur entwickelt.

Softwareentwicklung

  • Entwicklung TypeScript-basierter Automatisierungen und Services entlang unserer gesamten Wertschöpfungskette im HubSpot CRM

  • Entwicklung von HubSpot-Apps und UI Extensions (React) für unsere internen Teams – von CRM-Cards bis Workflow-Actions

  • Verwaltung von Scopes, Token-Rotation, App-Versionierung und Deployments (CI/CD)

Automatisierungen & Workflows

  • Entwicklung und Betrieb von Custom-Code-Automatisierungen, die als Teil von HubSpot-Workflows laufen – inklusive Pflege der Workflows selbst (Trigger, Enrollment-Kriterien, Fehlerbilder)

  • Bewusste Platzierung von Logik: Du entscheidest, was in einen Workflow gehört, was in Custom Code und was in einen Backend-Service – und migrierst Logik dorthin, wo sie testbar und wartbar ist

  • Analyse und Behebung von Incidents in der bestehenden Automatisierungslandschaft, inklusive Datenkorrekturen und Backfills per Skript

API- & Event-getriebene Architektur

  • Einsatz der HubSpot CRM APIs für Objekte, Assoziationen und Batch-Operationen

  • Nutzung von Webhooks & Subscriptions für Event-getriebene Synchronisation

  • Aufbau robuster Retry-, Error-Handling- und Monitoring-Mechanismen – inklusive bewusstem Umgang mit Rate-Limits und Datenvolumen

Datenmodellierung & CRM-Architektur

  • Definition von Objektbeziehungen, Ownership-Logiken und Lifecycle-Zuständen

  • Sicherstellung von Datenkonsistenz über mehrere Systeme hinweg

Integrationen & Plattform-Strategie

  • Technische Anbindung interner sowie externer Systeme (z.B. Abrechnung, Metering, Energie-Backends, eigener Tech Stack)

  • Aufbau sauberer Schnittstellen zwischen HubSpot und produktiven Kernsystemen

  • Aktive Mitgestaltung der langfristigen CRM- & Integrationsarchitektur – inklusive der schrittweisen Verlagerung komplexer Geschäftslogik aus Workflows in testbare Backend-Services



Dein Profil

Software-Engineering

  • Mindestens 5 Jahre Erfahrung in der Entwicklung von Web-Anwendungen, mit klarem Schwerpunkt Backend

  • Sehr gute Kenntnisse in TypeScript; solide React-Kenntnisse für unsere CRM-Cards und UI Extensions (NestJS ist ein Plus)

  • Erfahrung mit REST-APIs, asynchronen Systemen, Queues und Event-Verarbeitung

  • Verständnis für saubere API-Verträge, Versionierung und Testing – du weißt, wann ein Pattern hilft und wann es Zeremonie ist

Systemdenken: Automatisierung & Skalierung

  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung mit API- und Event-getriebener Integration von SaaS-Plattformen (CRM, Billing o.Ä.) – praktische Erfahrung mit der HubSpot Developer Platform (Private/Public Apps, OAuth 2.0, Scopes, Webhooks, UI Extensions) ist ein starkes Plus

  • Erfahrung im Design skalierbarer CRM- und Integrationsarchitekturen; du kannst HubSpot sinnvoll in eine größere Systemlandschaft einbetten

Arbeitsweise & Ownership

Wir bauen die Software, mit der Mieterstromprojekte laufen: Zählerdaten rein, Abrechnung raus, und alles dazwischen. Das Core Team verantwortet das Betreiberportal, das Produkt, auf dem der laufende Betrieb unserer Kunden steht. Es ist unser fachlich tiefstes Team, und es wächst.

Das Betreiberportal ist kein generisches SaaS. Es bildet die Energiewirtschaft ab: Messstellenbetrieb, Marktkommunikation, Netzentgelte, Umlagen, Abrechnung nach Regeln, die der Gesetzgeber schreibt und regelmäßig ändert. Wer hier priorisiert, muss verstehen, was eine Anforderung für den Betreiber wirtschaftlich bedeutet und was passiert, wenn sie falsch umgesetzt wird.

Dafür suchen wir eine Person, die das Team führt und das Geschäft dahinter versteht. Nicht als Durchreiche für Tickets und nicht als Architekt, der alles selbst entscheidet, sondern als jemand, der Business-Anforderungen in technische Entscheidungen übersetzt und dafür sorgt, dass gute Entwickler gute Arbeit machen können: klare Ziele, wenig Reibung, ehrliches Feedback, verlässliche Lieferung.

Der Weg dahin ist bewusst gewählt: Du startest für rund sechs Monate als Entwickler im Core Team. Du baust Features, machst Reviews und lernst Codebasis, Fachlichkeit und Menschen von innen kennen. Danach übernimmst du die Führung des Teams. Wer ein Team führen will, das er nie von innen gesehen hat, führt es an dem vorbei, was zählt.

Technisch: Python mit Django und Django Ninja im Backend, React mit TypeScript im Frontend, PostgreSQL mit TimescaleDB, deployt auf Kubernetes per GitOps mit ArgoCD. KI-Coding-Assistenten sind fester Teil des Workflows. In den ersten Monaten schreibst du diesen Code selbst. Danach musst du ihn weiter lesen können und verstehen, worüber dein Team diskutiert.

📈 Who We Are:

We are rebuilding the energy transaction, making it transparent and fair.

Our goal is to put power back where it belongs, in the hands of customers and to take on one of the most critical problems of our century, access to low cost electricity.

tem exists to fix a broken global energy market that’s long favoured legacy operators, intermediaries, and opaque pricing. Today’s electricity system was not designed for rapid decarbonisation, AI-driven efficiency or fair access for the actual users - businesses and generators.

We’ve built the first AI native transaction infrastructure to reinvent how electricity is bought, sold and priced. Our technology is designed to cut out the inefficient fees, automate complex market flows, and bring transparency and fairness to energy transactions at scale.

In late 2025, after extraordinary growth, we closed a $75 million Series B - led by Lightspeed Venture Partners with participation from Albion, Atomico, Allianz, Hitachi Ventures, Hitachi Ventures, Schroders Capital and others - positioning us for global expansion, deeper product innovation and category leadership.

We’re scaling internationally and building toward a future where AI-driven infrastructure is foundational to electricity markets worldwide.

Since launch, our modern utility product, known as RED, has already facilitated thousands of business customers and billions in energy transaction value, proving that modern software and AI can transform an industry built on legacy systems.

At tem, we’re not just building another energy company, we’re rearchitecting market infrastructure so that transparency, efficiency and sustainability become the default, not the exception.

The Role

We run multi-channel brand campaigns: social, content, video, out-of-home, events and road shows, often all at once. We've got plenty of ideas and a growing calendar. What we're missing is someone who owns delivery from the first brief to the final asset, across every channel. This is a hands-on generalist role.

Campaign ideas can come from the wider team (or yourself!), but you'll make it happen: the plan, the timeline, the budget, the agency or freelancer, the channel mix, the logistics when a campaign goes offline, and sometimes even copy or campaign set up. You organise and you do. You’re the connect point between Brand & Credibility and other teams, internal and external.

You'll work day to day with the Brand and Credibility team, our product marketers, and across tem's other teams as campaigns touch them. You will:

  • Own campaigns from brief to delivery across owned and offline channels, on brand, on time, on budget.

  • Plan and run events and support road shows.

  • Find, brief and manage agencies and freelancers: creative, media, production, experiential.

  • Keep multiple projects moving at once across teams that don't report to you.

  • Embed AI workflows or tooling to maximize efficiency and effectiveness in our service

Responsibilities

Campaign delivery

  • Build briefs, timelines and budget plans, then drive execution to completion.

  • Keep deliverables aligned across channels and accurate, working with product marketing to check every claim.

  • Spot and act on comms opportunities around key brand moments.

  • Align the Brand and Credibility campaign calendar with the rest of the business needs

  • Run a short post-campaign review each time so the next one is sharper.

Events and offline

  • Own roadshow support, customer events and out-of-home from planning through to the day itself, including the logistics.

  • Travel to events roughly once a month (a day or two, UK).

  • Manage merch and swag: design, ordering, distribution.

  • Support in the branding needs around our bi-annual internal company-wide event, temfest

Agencies and freelancers

  • Source and manage external partners, own the brief and artwork through to delivery, and hold them to time and budget.

  • Coordinate freelancer-led paid tests when we run them. You don't need to run paid yourself (but huge plus if you can).

Must haves

  • 2-4 years in a marketing, agency or creative production role where you delivered multi-channel campaigns or events end to end.

Bonus points

tem exists to fix a broken global energy market that’s long favoured legacy operators, intermediaries, and opaque pricing. Today’s electricity system was not designed for rapid decarbonisation, AI-driven efficiency or fair access for the actual users - businesses and generators.

We’re scaling internationally and building toward a future where AI-driven infrastructure is foundational to electricity markets worldwide.

At tem, we’re not just building another energy company, we’re rearchitecting market infrastructure so that transparency, efficiency and sustainability become the default, not the exception.

In short

We're looking for a Video Lead to shoot and edit for tem. Full-time, £70,000, based anywhere in the UK with shoots around the country.

tem connects businesses directly with the renewable generators that power them, which makes it an unusually diverse thing to film: solar and wind sites, the people who run them, the businesses buying from them, and the engineers building the technology in between. Here's some of what we've made so far: here, here, here and here.

The work we want to make

Two kinds of video, held to the same standard.

Considered films, where pacing, sound and framing carry the story and every shot is there for a reason. The kind someone who has never thought about energy watches to the end, because they've started to care about the person in it.

And social pieces that aren't templates: short cuts made with real intent, where the rhythm, timing, sound design and effects all serve the idea. Native to the platform, unmistakably crafted.

You'll move between the two in the same week without either one slipping.

If you're freelance - most of the best shooter-editors work for themselves, and we understand why. Here's what we'd want you to know.

This isn't corporate video. Generator stories, customer films, policy explainers, engineering pieces and people-led series - a social series one week, a customer film the next. When it's worth moving fast, we can go from idea to published within a week, if that’s what we collectively decide.

You'd be building something, not borrowing it. Rather than picking up someone else's style for a few weeks, you'd shape what tem's video looks and feels like, and build a body of work around it over years. You're expected, and encouraged, to argue when you see a better way.

Fewer feedback rounds. One brand, one small team, and a direct line to whoever wrote the brief. You learn tem once, properly.

The money. £70,000, stock options, paid holiday, and no invoices to chase or quiet months to plan around.

What you'll own

tem's video from first shot to final export: how it's planned, shot and cut, and how it looks and sounds across everything we publish. You'll sit in the Brand team and report into the Content Lead.

  • Shoots. Planning properly - schedule, kit, shot list, a recce where it's worth it - then staying alert on the day for what the plan couldn't know. Running most shoots solo, and knowing when a piece needs extra crew and when a phone and good instincts will do.

  • People. Most of the generators, engineers and finance directors you'll film have never been on camera. Putting them at ease and getting the real version of them is half the job.

  • The edit (around 70% of your week). Cutting, grading, mixing and titling in Premiere Pro. Giving short social pieces the same care as the long ones, letting the considered films breathe, and making something good from very little when there's no shoot.

  • Story and style. Turning a brief or rough idea into how it should be shot and sequenced, pushing back when you see a better version, and developing a visual language for tem video over time.

How we use AI (and how we don't)

We're not looking for someone to make AI-generated films - our content works because it's real. We use tools where they earn their place: transcription and paper edits, selects, audio clean-up, subtitles, cutdowns and versioning, the occasional fix in post, and pre-production like moodboards and storyboards. We want someone curious enough to try new tools, with the judgement to know when not to.

What we're looking for

Must haves

  • A portfolio, wherever it lives, that shows both halves: considered, human storytelling and social work cut with real intent.

  • A professional standard at both shooting and editing.

  • Speed without losing control.

  • The ability to plan and run a shoot yourself.

  • Good with people, on and off camera.

  • Sensible, hands-on use of AI tools in a real pipeline.

  • UK-based and happy to travel for shoots.

Bonus points

  • Premiere Pro, since it's what we cut in.

  • Colour, sound design or motion graphics beyond the basics.

  • A freelance or small-studio background.

  • An interest in energy, climate or tech.

What you get

  • £70,000 salary, reviewed twice a year.

  • Your say in what video kit we invest in for the content team.

  • Stock options so everyone has ownership in our mission.

  • 25 days holiday plus public holidays (swap them for the ones that matter to you), and your birthday off.

  • Remote first and flexible working, with no internal meetings on Friday afternoons.

  • Up to £1,200 a year for your remote setup and £150 a month for wellbeing.

How to apply

  • Send us your work. Your portfolio plus two recent pieces, with a line on what you did on each via the application form.

  • A 30-minute conversation with Alex (Content Lead) and Chelsea.

  • A paid, one-hour edit challenge. We send you unreleased tem footage, you cut it, and we talk through your choices. Everyone who delivers an edit at this stage is paid £200, hired or not - we don't think ideas should be taken for free.

  • A final conversation with leadership.

Our platform now powers Total Triage to manage patient demand, and Self-Book, which lets patients schedule their own appointments in seconds. We’ve automated routine care with Patient Questionnaires for long-term conditions, while Accumail finally allows staff-to-staff communication to happen instantly across different care settings. We’re now pushing the boundaries of the consultation itself with Accurx Scribe, our AI-powered note-taker that drafts medical notes in real-time.

We’re not just shipping features. We’re giving clinicians their time back and ensuring every patient journey is as smooth as it should be.

That sounds cool - what does a Customer Success Lead have to do with it?

Accurx works with 41 of the 42 NHS ICBs and is growing fast in secondary care. To keep up with how the NHS is organising itself, our Account Management team has just moved to a regional model, with leads for London, the South and the North. The goal is simple: join up what we’re learning across primary care, secondary care, acute, community and mental health, and make sure the best opportunities get surfaced across the whole of England, not just in one set of ICBs.

We’re hiring a Customer Success Lead for the North. You’ll lead a team of Customer Success Managers across primary and secondary care and be the strategic, zoomed-out view of the region. Your team is close to the accounts. Your job is to spot the patterns across them, turn what they’re hearing into strategy, and help Accurx show up at a regional level.

The challenges you’ll solve as a Customer Success Lead

  • Lead and grow a team of CSMs. You’ll start with three CSMs, each with their own region, customers and stage of the customer journey. You’ll coach them, unblock them and help them do the best work of their careers.

  • Bring two very different care settings together. Primary care is about deepening trust we’ve built over years. Secondary care is about firsts: new services, longer implementations and goalposts that move. You’ll work out what connects them, what doesn’t, and where learnings from one can speed up the other.

  • Turn insight into strategy. Your team will feed you what’s happening on the ground. You’ll spot trends, gaps and duplicated effort across the region and turn them into projects, goals and growth opportunities in products like Accurx Scribe and Total Triage.

  • Own the commercial picture for your region. You’ll keep a close eye on churn, risk, renewals and upsell across your team’s accounts, and represent the region at our weekly business reviews with the exec team.

  • Build the playbook with your fellow leads. The regional model is brand new. Alongside the leads for London and the South, you’ll shape how we work, what best practice looks like and how we scale it.

  • Be the link across the business. You’ll work closely with implementation, transformation, support and business development, making sure the voice of our customers shapes where Accurx goes next.


You should apply if...

  • You’ve led customer-facing teams. You have a few years of people management in customer success or account management, and you love helping others grow.

  • You’ve built things from the ground up. You’ve been on a startup to scale-up journey, worn a lot of hats, and taken customers from never having heard of you to being your biggest advocates.

  • You care about depth, not volume. You’ve looked after long-standing, strategic relationships rather than a high-volume queue, and you know that trust is what makes customers stick.

  • You can zoom out. You don’t need to be in the weeds of every account. You’re great at spotting patterns, asking the right questions and knowing where your team needs you most.

  • You’re comfortable with ambiguity. You’re happy to try something, get it wrong, learn and go again. Process is something you create, not something you wait for.

  • You’re a big collaborator. You’re an incredible communicator and listener, and you know the best outcomes come from working across teams.

  • You’re curious about the NHS. Healthcare experience is welcome but not essential. What matters is empathy for the pressure the NHS is under and the patience to build trust in a complex system.


What’s in it for me?

You’ll be joining an established but fast-growing Tech for Good movement, where we’re led by our Principles and our mission to Solve Healthcare Productivity.

  • £70,000 - £90,000 salary + share options up to £30,000

  • Benefits to suit you: adjust your healthcare cover, your pension or life insurance, whatever stage you’re at in life

  • Flexible Working: We are an office-first culture and ask that you’re in our (dog-friendly) Shoreditch office 3 days a week, with core hours of 10am-4pm

  • Time off: You’ll get 28 days of holiday (plus bank holidays) and up to 4 weeks to work from anywhere per year

  • Family matters: We offer enhanced parental leave, fertility support and parental loss support

  • We have our very own Chef! Free healthy breakfasts, snacks and lunches will be provided, with the occasional sweet treat!

Want to know more about the company or the hiring process? Check out our Careers page and Candidate hub.

Find us across social media: Medium, LinkedIn, X, Instagram and YouTube.

Diversity and Equal Opportunities: We are an equal opportunities employer and a pleasant and supportive place to work. We particularly welcome applications from those who are significantly underrepresented in the technology sector, such as women, non-binary people, transgender people, people with disabilities, LGBTQIA+ community and individuals from Black and Minority Ethnic communities.

jobs.title: GRC Security Specialist
jobs.description:
About Abound

We’re redefining consumer lending in the UK, and beyond. Using advanced AI and Open Banking data, we make fair, affordable personal finance available to more people. While traditional lenders rely almost entirely on credit scores, we look at the full financial picture - how much you spend, and what you can afford to repay to build a deeper, more accurate understanding of each customer's unique financial situation.


And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch.


Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us.

The role

We are formalising our security assurance function. We have technical controls and the engineering culture; what we need now is the governance layer that proves it - to our auditors, to our funders, and to our regulator.

You will be the delivery engine behind that. You will own the recurring assurance cycle end to end, run our third-party security programme, and be the person who turns evidence into something a due diligence team or a certification auditor can be satisfied by.

You will be responsible for building controls, gathering evidence, and challenging suppliers.

What you will own:

1. Third-party security assurance

- Run security due diligence on new suppliers, maintain initial questionnaire to risk sign-off, working with Procurement and Legal on security and data protection schedules.

- Maintain a supplier tiering model based on criticality and run the periodic re-assessment cycle for tiered suppliers: certification expiry, subprocessor changes, breach notifications, SLA performance.

- Maintain the supplier and outsourcing registers, including preparation for the FCA's material third party register under PS26/2 (rules in force 18 March 2027).

- Track concentration risk and exit plans for critical suppliers.

2. Inbound due diligence and customer assurance

- Own our response to security due diligence from funders, banking partners, institutional investors, commercial partners and prospects.

- Build and maintain a reusable trust pack: answer library, security whitepaper, current certifications, pen test attestations, standard questionnaire pre-fills (SIG, CAIQ).

- Turn a 40-hour bespoke questionnaire response into a 4-hour one.

3. The assurance calendar

- Maintain the annual calendar of security activities and make sure each one happens, produces evidence, and closes its actions: penetration tests, access reviews, disaster recovery tests, tabletop exercises, policy reviews, supplier re-assessments, awareness training.

- Coordinate external penetration tests: scoping, vendor selection, scheduling, findings triage, remediation tracking, retest.

- Facilitate tabletop exercises, including scenario design and post-exercise action tracking.

4. Risk and control administration

- Maintain the information security risk register: run the assessment cycle, record treatment plans with named owners and dates, chase closure.

- Administer the policy exception and risk acceptance process, ensuring every exception is owned, time-bound and reviewed on expiry.

- Perform first-line control testing: sample-test where key controls operate as designed and retain the evidence.

- Produce security MI for the Head of Security to take to ExCo and the Risk Committee.

5. Vulnerability and findings management

- Consolidate findings across sources — EDR, cloud security posture, SAST/DAST/SCA, secrets scanning, penetration tests — into a single view with agreed severity definitions and remediation SLAs.

- Triage, route and chase remediation with engineering teams; escalate ageing findings.

- Own the reporting on remediation performance.

6. Security awareness

- Run the awareness programme: induction, annual refresher, phishing simulation, role-based training for engineers, completion tracking.

- Coordinate pre-employment screening with People.

What you will contribute to:

- The ISO 27001 ISMS, which we are building towards certification. You will draft and maintain control documentation, populate the Statement of Applicability, gather evidence, coordinate the internal audit programme and be a primary point of contact for our external auditor. The Head of Security owns the framework, scope, and risk appetite.

- Policies and standards: you will draft, review and shepherd policies through approval, and track the review cycle.

- Incident response: you will maintain the IR plan and playbooks, facilitate post-incident reviews, track remediation actions, and support regulatory notification (ICO personal data breach reporting within 72 hours; FCA notification under Principle 11 / SUP 15.3).

- Business continuity and DR: you will maintain the documentation and the testing evidence.

- Secure development: you will help embed security requirements into the SDLC and support threat modelling sessions.

- Data protection: you will support RoPA maintenance, DPIA completion and DSAR handling alongside Legal.

What success looks like:

First 90 days: you know our supplier estate and have tiered it; the assurance calendar for the next 12 months is published and owned; inbound due diligence requests come to you and go out without the Head of Security rewriting them.

Six months: the trust pack exists and is being used; the risk register is live with owned treatment plans; ISO 27001 evidence collection is systematic rather than a scramble; the exception register exists.

Twelve months: supplier re-assessment runs on a cadence without prompting; the material third party register is ready ahead of the March 2027 deadline; MI to the Risk Committee is trusted.

Essential experience:

- Three or more years in an information security assurance, GRC or security compliance role, at least some of it in a regulated financial services environment or another environment with real external audit pressure.

- Hands-on experience of ISO 27001, whether operating an ISMS or taking one through certification.

- Demonstrable experience running third-party or vendor security assessments, and of responding to inbound security due diligence.

- Comfortable reading technical findings — an EDR vulnerability report, a penetration test finding, a cloud misconfiguration — and forming your own view on severity and real-world exploitability rather than passing the vendor's rating through unchanged.

- Clear, concise written English. Much of this role is writing things that external parties will judge us on.

- The confidence to chase a busy engineer, challenge a supplier's assertion, and tell us when an answer is not good enough.

Desirable:

- Experience of a cloud-native environment, ideally AWS.

- Experience of scaling a control framework as an organisation grows.

- Familiarity with UK operational resilience expectations (SYSC 15A) and outsourcing requirements (SYSC 8).

- Certifications such as CISM, CISA, ISO 27001 Lead Implementer or Lead Auditor, CRISC or CCSP. We care more about what you have done than what you hold.

jobs.title: Senior Electrical Characterisation Engineer
jobs.description:
About The Role and Team

Quantum Motion is a fast-growing quantum computing scale-up based in London founded by internationally renowned researchers from UCL and Oxford University with over 40 years’ experience in developing qubits and quantum computing architectures. Bringing together state-of-the-art cryogenic facilities and an outstanding interdisciplinary team, we are developing quantum processors based on industrial-grade silicon chips, with the potential to radically transform computing power in areas such as materials modelling, medicine, artificial intelligence and more.


Our Team


Since 2021 our team has been listed every year in the “Top 100 Startups worth watching” in the EE Times in 2021 and 2022, and our technology breakthroughs have been featured in The Telegraph, BBC and the New Statesman. Our founders are internationally renowned researchers from UCL and Oxford University who have pioneered the development of qubits and quantum computing architectures. Our chairman is the co-founder of Cadence and Synopsys, the two leading companies in the area of Electronic Design Automation. We’re backed by a team of top-tier investors, and we have recently closed our Series C funding of $160 million.

 

We bring together the brightest quantum engineers, integrated circuit (IC) engineers, quantum computing theoreticians and software engineers to create a unique, world-leading team, working together closely to maximise our combined expertise. Our collaborative and interdisciplinary culture is an ideal fit for anyone who thrives in a cutting-edge research and development environment focused on tackling big challenges and contributing to the development of scalable quantum computers based on silicon technology.

 

This is a rare and exciting opportunity to be an employee at a scale-up shaping the future of quantum computing. There are vast opportunities for professional growth and to make an impact within the company. 

Our team of 100+ is based across London, Oxford, San Sebastián and Sydney, with our primary hub in Islington (London).

We are looking for a Senior Electrical Characterisation Engineer to join our Process Integration team and play a key role in understanding, qualifying and improving the silicon devices at the heart of our quantum processors.

You will sit at a fascinating intersection between semiconductor manufacturing and quantum hardware, working closely with foundries, process engineers and quantum engineers.

You will use electrical characterisation and large-scale data analysis to understand manufacturing variability, identify the root causes of device behaviour, and feed those insights directly back into the semiconductor fabrication process.

This is an opportunity to have a tangible impact on the yield, quality and scalability of quantum processors, working with some of the most advanced silicon technology being developed for quantum computing.


Functions of the Role

  • Drive electrical characterisation of fabricated silicon devices, developing and continuously improving high-throughput screening methods to assess key device parameters including threshold voltage, gate oxide reliability and channel mobility.

  • Turn electrical data into manufacturing insight, identifying patterns, variability and device failures and connecting them back to semiconductor process steps such as photolithography, etching, oxide growth, CMP and doping.

  • Develop automated measurement and test infrastructure, creating robust Python-based test routines and instrument-control workflows across room-temperature and, where appropriate, low-temperature wafer probing environments.

  • Analyse large-scale electrical datasets using statistical process control, yield analysis and other data-driven techniques to monitor wafer uniformity, defect density and process drift.

  • Work directly with semiconductor foundries and process engineers, providing clear, actionable feedback that can be used to improve device performance, consistency and yield.

  • Build scalable characterisation processes, establishing testing standards, calibration procedures, SOPs and data pipelines that allow information to flow effectively between semiconductor process integration and quantum engineering teams.

  • Help shape how we characterise the next generation of our technology, bringing your expertise and ideas to continuously improve our measurement capability as Quantum Motion scales.

  • We are looking for someone who combines strong semiconductor device knowledge with a practical, data-driven approach to electrical characterisation.


Experience - Essentials


  • Master's or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Microelectronics, Semiconductor Physics, Materials Science or a closely related discipline.

  • 3+ years' experience in semiconductor device testing, reliability engineering, electrical characterisation or yield analysis within a foundry, IDM or semiconductor R&D environment.

  • Strong understanding of silicon CMOS fabrication processes, semiconductor device physics and foundry workflows.

  • Hands-on experience with semiconductor parameter analysers, SMUs and wafer probe stations, including DC and/or RF electrical testing.

  • Strong Python skills, particularly for instrument control, automation and automated test execution.

  • A highly analytical approach and the ability to work with large datasets to identify trends, anomalies and root causes.

  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across semiconductor, process, hardware and quantum engineering teams.


Experience - Desirable

It would be particularly valuable if you also have experience in:

  • Quantum device physics, including quantum dots, single-electron transistors (SETs) or charge-stability mapping.

  • Cryogenic electrical characterisation and low-temperature measurement systems.

  • Semiconductor yield improvement, process control or statistical analysis.

  • Automated wafer-level testing and high-throughput characterisation.

  • Working with advanced or emerging semiconductor technologies.


Benefits

  • Be part of a creative, world-leading team

  • Competitive salary and share options scheme

  • Contributory pension scheme

  • Group private medical insurance scheme

  • Life Assurance

  • Cycle-to-work Scheme 

  • Central London location


EEO Statement

Quantum Motion is committed to providing equal employment opportunity and does not discriminate based on age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, race, colour, religion, disability status, marital status, pregnancy, gender reassignment or any other protected characteristics covered by the Equality Act 2010.

  • Sugar Reduction & Product Performance: You develop reduced-sugar and no-added-sugar products without compromising on taste. You understand how ingredients affect texture, processing, stability and shelf life, and make clear trade-offs between quality, cost, compliance and speed.

  • Sensory, Shelf Life & Scale-Up: You plan and coordinate sensory, shelf-life and stability testing. You prepare for pilot and industrial trials, work closely with co-manufacturers, troubleshoot issues and follow solutions through to production.

  • Strong knowledge of sugar reduction, sweetener systems, fibres and texture management.

  • Experience planning, conducting or interpreting sensory tests, shelf-life studies and stability testing.

  • Background in better-for-you food, functional food, private-label NPD, or a fast-growing consumer brand.

  • Experience delivering products into D2C and retail channels across DACH or Europe.

Working at ahead is more than just a job - it’s your opportunity to develop as a professional and as a person, while shaping the future of snacking. You’ll become part of a team where international talent, startup drive, real impact, and true ownership come together.

About us

Since then, NET CHECK has developed into the leading partner of network operators and infrastructure providers of mobile and fixed networks of all technologies. We are looking for an Applied AI Scientist who combines strong analytical thinking with practical engineering skills. You will model complex problems, develop and prototype ML and agentic AI solutions, and turn them into reliable, production-ready tools for real users while applying the latest developments in AI.


Responsibilities

Your profile

  • Minimum 3 years of experience developing software or machine learning systems in an industry or research environment, alongside or following your studies.

jobs.title: Senior Process Engieer
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

tozero is Europe’s leading deep-tech startup specializing in the recycling of
lithium-ion batteries. Committed to accelerating decarbonization and transforming
the material life cycle, we’re actively crafting sustainable recycling solutions for a
cleaner and more innovative future.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for a Senior Process Engineer to take a leading technical role in the
design, scale-up, commissioning and ramp up of our battery recycling processes.
This role sits at the intersection of technology development, process engineering,
and industrial scale-up. You will translate experimental and operational data into
robust process designs, challenge engineering assumptions, and ensure that our
future plants are built on solid fundamentals.
Your focus will be on the processes that matter most to our technology — graphite
and lithium extraction. By working closely with R&D, Operations and external
engineering partners, you will actively lead and engage in activities associated with:
a) engineering design; b) commissioning and ramp up; c) process development.
We are looking for someone who is comfortable working in a production
environment, but who can also take a step back and understand what the data is
telling us, and engineer the process we need at different scales.


WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT

Must Have's:
1. Future Plant Design & Scale-up
● Own key process design activities for our next-generation plants.
● Develop and review PFDs, P&IDs, mass and energy balances, process
descriptions and equipment specifications for future capacity expansions.

● Translate pilot and industrial operating data into reliable engineering design
criteria and scale-up assumptions.
● Perform process calculations and equipment sizing to ensure our future
plants are designed based on validated engineering data rather than
theoretical assumptions alone.
2. Targeted Process Expertise & Optimization
● Become a technical reference for some of our most critical process steps.
● Apply strong chemical engineering fundamentals to the optimization of
graphite and lithium extraction and post-processing.
● Identify the parameters controlling yield, purity and process stability and
translate these insights into concrete process improvements.
● Work closely with R&D and Operations while maintaining a strong focus on
process performance and technology development rather than daily
troubleshooting.
3. Data Analysis & Process Modeling
● Turn plant data into engineering decisions.
● Evaluate operational and experimental data, build and validate mass balances
and process models, and identify gaps between expected and actual process
performance.
● Define what data needs to be collected to support future scale-up decisions.
● Technically guide data analysts and other engineering functions to ensure
that models and analytics remain grounded in physical and chemical reality.
● Translate analysis into clear recommendations for process upgrades and
future plant designs.
4. Commissioning & Process Validation
● Make sure what we designed actually works.
● Participate in FATs/SATs, commissioning activities and process performance
validation for new equipment and plant expansions.
● Develop acceptance and process validation criteria based on the original
design intent.
● Evaluate commissioning and operational data to confirm that installed
systems achieve their calculated performance targets.
● Work closely with Operations during handover while ensuring clear ownership
transfers once the process meets its design criteria.
5. Operational Readiness, Process Safety & SOPs
● Design processes that can be operated safely and consistently.
● Translate process design and engineering intent into clear Standard Operating
Procedures (SOPs), operating envelopes and process documentation.
● Participate actively in HAZOPs, LOPAs, and other process safety reviews,
ensuring that process risks are identified and addressed during design rather
than after installation.
● Support Operations in understanding the design basis and critical process
parameters of newly commissioned systems.

Nice-to-have's:
Vendor & EPC Coordination
● Represent tozero's process requirements with external engineering partners
and equipment suppliers.
● Prepare and review technical specifications, vendor proposals and engineering
documentation.
● Challenge unsupported assumptions, identify over-engineered solutions and
ensure equipment is correctly sized for our process.
● Support technical bid evaluations and equipment selection, balancing process
performance, CAPEX, operability and scalability.
● Act as a strong technical counterpart to EPCs, engineering contractors and
equipment vendors throughout project execution.


Your profile

You have a strong chemical/process engineering foundation and enjoy solving
technically complex problems with a combination of first-principles engineering and
real plant data.
● Degree in Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, Metallurgical
Engineering or a related technical field.
● Ideally 5+ years of experience in process engineering within the chemical,
hydrometallurgy, battery, mining, minerals, recycling or related process
industries; specific expertise in graphite and lithium extraction and
post-processing is highly preferred.
● Strong experience with process design and scale-up, including PFDs, P&IDs,
mass/energy balances and equipment sizing.
● Comfortable working with industrial datasets and translating operational data
into engineering models and decisions.
● Experience with solid-liquid separation, precipitation, flotation,
hydrometallurgy or mineral processing is highly valuable.
● Able to critically review vendor proposals and confidently challenge technical
assumptions.
● Strong experience supporting commissioning and process validation of
industrial equipment or plants.
● Familiarity with process safety methodologies such as HAZOP and LOPA.
● Comfortable moving between detailed calculations, engineering
documentation and the actual plant.
● Strong communicator who can work effectively across R&D, Engineering,
Operations, suppliers and EPC partners.
● Fluent English; German is a plus.


Why us?

Our technology is moving from first-of-a-kind industrial operations toward
increasingly larger and more standardized plants.
The Senior Process Engineer will help us make that transition successfully: turning
what we learn from today's plant into the engineering basis for tomorrow's plants
while supporting commissioning and ramping up efforts.
You will directly influence process performance, equipment selection, CAPEX and the
technical architecture of our future facilities — helping ensure that every new scale is
safer, simpler, more efficient and better engineered than the one before it.

jobs.description:
Who we are:

We're one of Europe's fastest-growing fintech companies – on a mission to create the world's most empowering way to pay.

We launched the product in 2020 and achieved double unicorn status, valued at $2 billion, and since then have taken on more than 6 million customers.

 

Our mission is to become the best way to pay for anything, anywhere and say goodbye to credit costs for everyone. This is huge. Want to join us?

About the role.

We are looking for a dynamic Legal Counsel, with circa 1-4 years PQE, to play a vital role in providing legal support and advice to our organisation as we continue to expand our operations in the UK and internationally. You will work closely with other members of our Legal team and teams across the business to advise on a broad range of legal matters, including arrangements with our commercial partners, corporate transactions and governance initiatives, and help ensure that we continue to comply with relevant laws and regulations in the UK and across international markets.

You’ll have an interest in a varied workload, with strong drafting and negotiating skills, sound commercial judgment, and the ability to balance legal risk with business priorities. You’ll be proactive and hands-on in your approach, happy to get stuck into a broad range of legal work, able to work independently while knowing when to escalate, and capable of building trust with business teams.

In addition, you’ll have a focus on developing and maintaining the legal processes, policies and precedents that underpin our business.

This is a fantastic opportunity if you enjoy operating in a fast-paced, growing business where priorities can change quickly, and are looking to take real ownership for what you do.

Day to day responsibilities.

  • Work with our business teams to draft, review and negotiate a wide range of commercial agreements, and other legal documents with third parties, including our key suppliers and partners, whilst maintaining the processes that underpin them.

  • Support with corporate matters including acquisitions, capital raising, group structure and integration projects, international expansion, debt arrangements and employee share schemes.

  • Support with governance and investor relations initiatives, including the preparation of board and committee papers and resolutions, updating our cap table and maintaining internal trackers.

  • Assist in resolving legal disputes, including working with external counsel when necessary.

  • Be a trusted legal advisor to our commercial teams to help establish, maintain, and expand business relationships whilst providing input into new products and initiatives.

  • Identify legal risks and propose strategies to mitigate them.

  • Support the consideration and implementation of new legal tech tools and the development and maintenance of processes, policies and procedures and standard legal documents.

  • Conduct legal research on various topics, including emerging legal issues which may impact our business, and provide recommendations to the legal team and senior management.

  • Develop and deliver legal training programmes to internal teams to ensure awareness of legal and regulatory requirements.

Key requirements:

  • Ideally, 1-4 years PQE.

  • A current practising certificate (qualified in England and Wales is preferred).

  • Meaningful and relevant experience either from private practice or in-house.

  • Experience gained in a fintech or another fast-paced technology business or internationally would be a bonus, but otherwise you should be able to demonstrate enthusiasm for gaining that experience.

  • Solid drafting, reviewing, negotiation and problem-solving skills.

  • Solutions-focused attitude, with a commercial-minded risk appetite.

  • Excellent attention to detail.

  • Strong stakeholder and time-management skills, including the ability to manage competing priorities

jobs.description:
Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe!

Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy.

We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

🐙 Kraken Generation Flex

The energy industry is undergoing the largest transformation since industrialisation, at an unprecedented rate of change and we are positioning ourselves at the heart of it. In the UK, with a legally binding Net Zero target for 2050 and a clean-power ambition for 2030, we are scaling rapidly to integrate Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) into the grid.

Kraken is recognised as a thought leader and innovator. With complete independence from Octopus Energy, we are building a SaaS business that digitally connects hundreds of thousands of DERs with energy markets. As our UK fleet grows and we support our expansion across Europe, we are looking for an Integrations Engineer to help turn customer sites into market-connected, controllable assets.

🏠 Where you’ll fit in and role summary

As we scale our fleet of integrated assets, we are looking for an Electrical Engineer to support the delivery of our site integrations and grow into owning them, learning the full lifecycle from the early information stage through design, deployment and testing.

You’ll be part of an engineering delivery team, based in Manchester, who take an integration project from the very early information stage, design how it will be integrated into Kraken’s platform and then turn that design into a live, controllable, market-participating asset.

Engineering delivery is an innovative and engineering-focused team with a culture that fosters collaboration and fresh thinking to create a new energy system. Alongside design, deployment and testing; they constantly look into ways to improve efficiency through tooling and the automation of repetitive tasks. They collaborate daily with delivery managers and customer success to onboard new sites as well as support the existing.

🚀 What you'll own

  • Integration design contribution: With guidance, analyse provided information and contribute to hardware and software integration approaches. When necessary, exchange information with customer technical representatives through meetings and emails, and take part in design discussions with other team members.

  • Technical judgement: Develop your technical judgement, making well-reasoned decisions and trade-offs with support from senior engineers, and contributing technical input to discussions within the team.

  • Developing domain knowledge: Build up your knowledge in one or more technical areas. This could include grid regulations (G99, G100, Grid Code etc.), energy markets, multi BMUs, industrial communication protocols, industrial networking, internet of things, cyber security and so on.

  • Gateway application & configuration: Learn how the Gateway software (developed by an internal software team) works and how it is configured. Understand the requirements for an integration and judge if the gateway software is able to support it or will need new development work. The team will help you get gateway configuration literate and you will carry out deployments and changes independently over time.

  • Hardware and Software Deployments: Learn the process of our hardware and software deployments. Over time, take ownership of the configuration, deployment and testing with guidance from the senior engineers.

  • Networking and cyber security: Contribute to hardware and network connectivity designs, keeping our own cyber security posture in mind as well as addressing the concerns from customers, with the support of the internal security team.

  • Site testing & commissioning: Carry out site testing and commissioning initially with the support of the team and building toward doing this independently as onboarding demand grows.

  • Incidents & compliance: Help address engineering help requests from other teams and support incident response in the case of issues at existing sites.

🧠 What you'll bring to the party

  • Understanding of the Regulations: Working knowledge of the UK Grid Code, G99 and the other obligations of a grid-connected asset before it can participate in the energy markets.

  • Understanding of the UK Energy Markets: Working understanding of the NESO ancillary services (Dynamic Containment / Moderation / Regulation, Firm Frequency Response), the Balancing Mechanism, and the DNO connection/integration process.

  • Technical judgement: Sound technical judgement and a structured approach to problems, working with the team to agree and implement a solution.

  • Power plant systems: Ability to read and analyse single line diagrams for a given power plant to understand the site architecture for the points of metering and control instrumentation.

  • Asset integration: Exposure to, or a keen interest in, integrating BESS (grid-scale and/or C&I) and/or RES (Wind and Solar) for telemetry and control.

  • Integration design: Ability to contribute to clear integration designs and design documentation.

  • Hardware and Networking: Familiarity with control systems deployments and their connectivity including the local networking and cyber security aspects, and an ability to help debug site connectivity and networking issues (including 4G routers and firewalls) with support.

  • Industrial Communication Protocols: Practical experience or a good working knowledge of Modbus (TCP/RTU); awareness of one or more of IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61400-25, OPC-UA or DNP3 is a plus.

  • CAD, Diagrams and Tools: Experience or familiarity with CAD tools such as AutoCAD or BricsCAD, Miro and Notion.

  • Communication: A clear communicator who documents their work (e.g. in design docs and Notion) and collaborates well with the team.

  • Commissioning landscape: Awareness of the other parties involved in site commissioning for power plants, their roles and responsibilities, and how we work with them.

  • Engineering background: Bachelor's in Electrical Engineering, Automation/Control, Software, or a related field - or equivalent practical experience in industrial/energy integration.

  • A proactive and collaborative mindset: You are eager to learn and grow, reliable and collaborative. You take initiative, communicate openly, raise risks early, and care about safe working. You welcome feedback, support your teammates, and steadily build toward taking on more independent ownership of integrations over time.

  • Travel: Willingness to travel to customers and sites although travel is very occasional. Awareness of site safety is required as we may work with site personnel even though we are remote.

⭐️ Bonus points

  • Wider knowledge of grid compliance (G99, G100, Grid Code) and where the Kraken system fits in.

  • Experience with AWS IoT Greengrass or similar edge-deployment architectures.

  • Familiarity with software/scripting and templating (e.g. Python, Rust, the Linux command line) and Git-based workflows.

  • Understanding of IT/OT security in the energy sector (IEC 62443, NIS Regulations awareness).

  • Exposure to wider European balancing markets / ENTSO-E frameworks and TSO integrations.
